_doc: Revert-verify mutants for issue #4268 (PR fix/4268-shacl-datatype-range). Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute). The diff restores the symmetry the file already DECLARES at XSD_DATATYPE_PREFIXES ('Range entries with these prefixes are sh:datatype constraints (apply to Literals). All other range entries are sh:class constraints (apply to IRI nodes only)') — the Literal branch implemented its half (filter the range down to datatype entries, skip when none remain), the IRI branch did not. Judging an IRI against `xsd:string` AS A CLASS is false BY CONSTRUCTION — nothing is an instance of a datatype — so that check could never go green for any data; it produced 9 violations in 2 nodes on vault-exodev under 16.240.18 where 16.240.16 had none. Guards enumerated per integration-test-revert-verify §A8: the filter expression (M1), the skip guard (M3), and the three sites that report the surviving expectation (M4 violation message, M5 unresolvable-ref message, M6 expectedRange). Expectations were derived axis-by-axis from what each axis ASSERTS, not from the mutant's theme (§A44). ⛔ ONE conceivable mutation carries no mutant, and the reason is collateral, not equivalence: inverting the filter polarity (`!isXSDDatatypeIRI` → `isXSDDatatypeIRI`) strips the CLASS entries instead, so every class-only range in the file empties and the skip guard swallows it — that reddens most of the suite (T25, T27+, Suite 8, the cross-vault and pilot suites) and its red set is dominated by collateral. It locks nothing that M1 does not already lock, so it is documented rather than written. ⛤ T74 is the control for the untouched Literal branch and stays GREEN under every mutant here — the stronger claim (§A37). Its non-vacuity is not assumed: it ACTUALLY reddened during development, when its first fixture self-tagged the literal (`'not-a-number'^^xsd:integer` under range xsd:integer) and `literalConformsToDatatype` short-circuited to true on `literalDatatype === expected`, never reaching the lexical judgement. The committed fixture tags the literal `xsd:string` so the lexical path runs.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/services/ShaclLiteValidator.ts

M1_filter_removed._note: Exactly the pre-fix behaviour: the IRI branch judges the value against every range entry, datatypes included.

M3_skip_guard_removed._note: Filtering still happens, but a range left with NO class entry no longer short-circuits: the value is checked against an empty expectation and can never conform.

M4_violation_message_join._note: The class-violation message again names the datatype entry it did not judge against.
M4_violation_message_join.from: `sh:class violation: <${obj.value}> does not conform to expected class ${classRanges.join(' | ')}`,
M4_violation_message_join.to: `sh:class violation: <${obj.value}> does not conform to expected class ${shape.range.join(' | ')}`,

M5_unresolvable_message_join._note: Same, on the unresolvable-ref warning path.
M5_unresolvable_message_join.from: ? `sh:class unresolvable-ref: <${obj.value}> has no resolvable type in this vault (cross-vault, symbolic, or external reference); not validated against ${classRanges.join(' | ')}`
M5_unresolvable_message_join.to: ? `sh:class unresolvable-ref: <${obj.value}> has no resolvable type in this vault (cross-vault, symbolic, or external reference); not validated against ${shape.range.join(' | ')}`

M6_expected_range_join._note: The machine-readable field consumers filter on (`expectedRange`) again carries the datatype entry.
